clue.text: Hot drink for one in Students Union

indicators.note: the example abbreviation sits in the union's initials, so in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
for one means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A student asks for a warming drink at the union bar.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS is Britain's National Union of Students. The drink is an old mix of hot wine, sugar and spices.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spiced wine punch, named after an eighteenth-century colonel, is the drink in question.

clue.text: Note about bank worker who needs holiday accommodation?

indicators.note: about tells us the musical note is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: SOH is a spelling of sol, the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale
a teller pays out and takes in money at a bank counter

explanation.surface: A musician asks a bank cashier about somewhere to stay on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In tonic sol-fa the fifth note can be spelt 'soh'; 'about' turns it round. The definition describes the person who stays at youth hostels.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller lodging cheaply at youth hostels is the person seeking such holiday lodging.

clue.text: Popular officer more often than not

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked officer is someone who is usually around, a phrase that barely holds together as a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for usually, as a rule, on most occasions.

clue.text: Maybe a participant in highland games races here

parts.note: Highland games are Scottish athletic gatherings, so a competitor might be a Scot; Maybe flags the example

explanation.surface: A caber-tosser at a Scottish highland gathering might enter a race there.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the Berkshire racecourse famous for Royal Ascot week.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire course hosts famous horse races, so it is a place where racing happens.

clue.text: Man behind old shelter protected by safe electrical device

indicators.note: the safe guards the other pieces, so protected by puts them inside it

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: behind places the island after the old shelter

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man sheltering in an old tent is kept safe beside some electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, IOM. PETER is old underworld slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures voltage or acts as a variable resistor, so it is a piece of electrical equipment.

clue.text: See what is signified by green trademark

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: Someone tries to read the meaning behind a company's green brand mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's emblem or symbol serves as its trademark, identifying its products.

clue.text: Little Jack's habit, once?

parts.note: Jack is a sailor (Jack Tar) and a habit is clothing; little boys were once dressed in naval outfits

explanation.surface: It seems to ask about a small boy's former routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a behaviour but means a garment, and Jack Tar is a sailor; Victorian boys commonly wore such outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Children were once dressed in naval-style blue and white outfits, a miniature version of a seaman's garb.

clue.text: Mocking horrible giants, divine female messenger intervenes

indicators.note: the messenger comes between the jumbled letters, so intervenes means inserted
horrible suggests the giants are mangled into a new order

parts.note: Iris was the messenger goddess of Greek myth

explanation.surface: Horrible giants are being mocked, and a goddess carrying messages steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges the giants into SATING, and the Greek messenger goddess 'intervenes', splitting that anagram after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampooning someone with ridicule or irony means mocking them.

clue.text: Steal from till if tempted

indicators.note: from tells us to take the letters out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A shop worker is tempted to steal from the cash register.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch or pilfer something is slang for stealing it, as in shoplifting.

clue.text: Synod's main row must be resolved explicitly

indicators.note: resolved, in the sense of broken down and reworked, signals rearranging these letters

explanation.surface: A church synod's chief quarrel has to be settled openly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means saying something directly and plainly, without hinting.

clue.text: Run into stake in ancient cave

indicators.note: into places the run abbreviation inside the stake

parts.note: the ante is the stake put up in poker
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs a wooden stake into an old cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a literary, archaic word for a cave, hence 'ancient'.
explanation.definitionFit: This poetic, old-fashioned word for a cavern is used by Shakespeare in Othello.

clue.text: Soldier eats a dirty biscuit

indicators.note: the soldier takes the other pieces inside, so eats signals containment

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A soldier munches a filthy biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The biscuit is a British currant biscuit, named after the Italian patriot.
explanation.definitionFit: This British biscuit with a layer of squashed currants is named after the Italian hero.

clue.text: Female servant in dismay, badly treated by stable servant?

indicators.note: by, as in held by, puts the jumble inside the stable hand

parts.note: a stable lad looks after racehorses

indicators.note: badly treated signals that the word dismay is knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A maid is upset at being mistreated by a stable hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly treated' rearranges the word dismay into DYSMAI, which 'by' (held by) puts inside a stable lad, a worker who tends racehorses.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid is a personal attendant to a woman, a female domestic.

clue.text: State times to have drinks brought round

indicators.note: the drinks are brought round the multiplication sign, so it ends up inside them

parts.note: teas are cups of tea
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Every so often a state arranges for drinks to be carried round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Star State is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: What may add colour to digital presentation?

definitions.text: What may add colour to digital presentation?

parts.words: What may add colour to digital presentation?
parts.note: digital refers to fingers (digits), not computers; the varnish colours fingertips

explanation.surface: It sounds like advice on brightening up an on-screen slide show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' points to computers but means fingers: digits.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured varnish painted on fingertips brightens how one's hands look.

clue.text: Stage performance? Only half laugh

indicators.note: only half keeps the front half of the word for laugh

explanation.surface: A comic's stage show gets only half a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Halve GIGGLE to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a single booked show by a band or comedian, a performance on stage.

clue.text: Young male, worker perhaps, voiced sound

parts.note: a son is a young male child
a worker is one kind of ant, so ant is an example

explanation.surface: A young man, perhaps a labourer, speaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics the term names a voiced speech sound, one made with the vocal cords vibrating.

clue.text: They are bullying boatman to secure a level of proficiency

indicators.note: the boatman holds the grade inside him, so to secure signals containment

parts.note: Harris is one of the three men in Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat
a dan is a grade of skill in judo or karate

explanation.surface: Bullies are pressing a ferryman to reach a certain skill grade.
explanation.walkthrough: The boatman is Harris from the comic novel Three Men in a Boat; DAN is a martial-arts grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewish, domineering old women are bossy and overbearing, so they bully people.

clue.text: American uncle entertaining the French somewhere in Massachusetts

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An American uncle plays host to French visitors at a town in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: The New England town famous for its 1692 witch trials lies in that state.

clue.text: Demanding types who look back on dramatic careers?

definitions.meaning: people who demand or extort payment

definitions.text: who look back on dramatic careers?

explanation.surface: Pushy people reminisce about their stage careers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as EX-ACTORS for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who exact, extorting money or obedience, are demanding; split up, the word gives former thespians.

clue.text: Designer about to get into new role, having more work?

indicators.note: the abbreviation enters the jumbled letters, so to get into signals insertion
new means the letters of role are made afresh in another order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, about
someone with more work is busier

explanation.surface: A designer moving to a new job expects to be busier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROLE into LEOR, and C ('about', from circa) goes into it to give LECOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss-French modernist was a renowned architect and furniture designer.

clue.text: Register one group of soldiers turning up with another

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read the letters upwards, backwards

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
TA is the Territorial Army, another body of soldiers

explanation.surface: One unit of troops arrives along with another to enrol.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) and TA (Territorial Army) are British military abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster or list of people's turns of duty is a register of sorts.

clue.text: It's mean, affording dukes minimal space?

definitions.meaning: dukes is slang for fists, so fists held tightly

explanation.surface: Someone complains about cramped lodgings given to aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dukes' are not nobles but fists, as in 'put up your dukes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stingy, unwilling to spend money, is the everyday sense; literally, hands clenched tight.

clue.text: Figures, still small, first to be accepted

indicators.note: the ordinal is taken in by the other pieces, so to be accepted signals insertion

parts.note: static means still, not moving
1ST, with I for the digit 1, is first

explanation.surface: Small and still numbers are put forward to be approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1ST, written IST with I standing for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerical data collected and analysed are figures.

clue.text: Number line up on step briefly in old city

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nine is a number

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a grade is a step or stage

explanation.surface: Numbers line up on a short step in an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NINE L into LENIN; 'briefly' cuts GRADE to GRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: St Petersburg bore this name in Soviet times, so it is a former name of a city.

clue.text: Administrators offering support within and support without

indicators.note: within says the first support goes inside
without, in its old sense of outside, places the second support around

parts.note: a truss is a supporting framework or bandage
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: Administrators back people both inside and outside the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, as in the hymn 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who manage property or funds on behalf of others act as administrators.

clue.text: Worthless idiot has taken in old boy

indicators.note: the idiot takes the old boy inside, signalling containment

parts.note: a twit is a fool
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A useless fool has been conned by a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap or trifling, worth only a couple of bits, is American slang for valueless.

clue.text: Hot rock periodical being copied, almost

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter
being copied means the word for periodical is written twice

parts.note: mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A geology magazine is being photocopied, nearly all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being copied' writes MAG twice, and 'almost' cuts the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten material beneath the earth's crust is hot liquid rock.

clue.text: Report of bitterness in land taken by Romans

indicators.note: report means a spoken account, so it signals a word that sounds the same

parts.note: gall means bitterness or rancour

explanation.surface: News of bitter feelings in territory captured by Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar conquered this ancient region, roughly modern France.

clue.text: Soft fibres covering the top

indicators.note: covering the top hides the head of the word, so its first letter disappears

parts.note: flax is the fibre used to make linen

explanation.surface: Soft fibres are laid over the top of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering the top' hides the first letter of FLAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack, lenient, not strict: soft in the sense of easygoing.
